conbody.p: The UNPIVOT clause transforms structured data sets by merging multiple columns into a single data column while generating a corresponding header column for the original source attributes.

The UNPIVOT clause is a query operator that allows you to reorganize data by merging multiple columns from a table into a single data column. This process creates a more normalized result set by rotating columns into rows, making the data easier to aggregate or analyze.

When you apply the UNPIVOT clause to a table reference, the following changes occur:
The query engine merges specified UNPIVOT columns from the source table into a single data column.
The result table includes a new header column that identifies the original source column for every row.
All original columns that are not part of the UNPIVOT definition are retained in the result set.
For each row in the source table, the operation generates one row in the result table for every specified unpivot column.

The following syntax block shows the structure of a UNPIVOT operation:SELECT columns FROM table_name UNPIVOT ( data_column FOR header_column IN ( column_x [AS label_x], column_y [AS label_y], ...) ) [AS] result_alias;

note.p: The result_alias is mandatory. Only the AS keyword is optional.
The table_name in the FROM clause must reference a table, view, or WITH clause directly. Subqueries and table aliases are not supported on the UNPIVOT source. The following are syntax errors:

ul.li: SELECT * FROM (SELECT ...) s UNPIVOT (...) AS t; - subquery as source
SELECT * FROM tbl s UNPIVOT (...) AS t; - table with alias

conbody.p: When you use the UNPIVOT clause, keep the following details in mind:

ul.li: The AS clause in the IN list is optional. Without AS, the column name becomes the label as a string. With AS, the label can be any literal value (string, number, or other literal), but all labels in the same UNPIVOT clause must be literals of the same data type. If labels have different data types, the query fails with the error Expressions for the UNPIVOT header column should have the same type. Multiple columns can have the same label, but the same column cannot be listed more than once in the IN clause.
You cannot directly resolve or select the original source columns after performing the UNPIVOT operation.

Rows are generated for NULL values as well, so the data column contains NULL for them. Unlike some other databases, Impala has no INCLUDE NULLS or EXCLUDE NULLS option. To drop rows with NULL values in the data column, add WHERE data_column IS NOT NULL to the query.

conbody.p:
The following example shows a UNPIVOT operation that merges two INT columns into one. The source is a temporary table defined in a WITH clause: WITH t1 (a, v1, v2) AS ( VALUES (1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6) ) SELECT * FROM t1 UNPIVOT ( c FOR b IN (v1 AS 'v1', v2 AS 'v2') ) AS t;
+---+---+----+ | a | c | b | +---+---+----+ | 1 | 2 | v1 | | 1 | 3 | v2 | | 4 | 5 | v1 | | 4 | 6 | v2 | +---+---+----+

ul.li: The WITH clause defines a temporary table t1 with three columns: a, v1, and v2.
The UNPIVOT clause merges the unpivot columns v1 and v2 into a single data column c.
The header column b contains the string labels 'v1' or 'v2' to indicate the source of the data for each row.
Column a is retained in the result because it is not part of the UNPIVOT definition.
The result set contains one row for each combination of the original row and each unpivot column.

conbody.p: All UNPIVOT columns must share an identical data type.
Workaround: Cast the columns to the same data type in a Common Table Expression (CTE), then apply UNPIVOT to the CTE.
Run the following query to align data types:
conbody.codeblock:
WITH t1 (a, v1, v2) AS ( VALUES (1, 2, 3.0) ), t1_casted AS ( SELECT a, CAST(v1 AS DECIMAL(2, 1)) AS v1, CAST(v2 AS DECIMAL(2, 1)) AS v2 FROM t1 ) SELECT * FROM t1_casted UNPIVOT ( c FOR b IN (v1 AS 'v1', v2 AS 'v2') ) AS t;
+---+-----+----+ | a | c | b | +---+-----+----+ | 1 | 2.0 | v1 | | 1 | 3.0 | v2 | +---+-----+----+ Fetched 2 row(s) in 0.11s
conbody.p: Each UNPIVOT clause must use a unique path expression because Impala does not support duplicate path expressions across multiple UNPIVOT clauses in the same query block.
Workaround: Define a CTE over one of the tables, and use it as the source of one of the UNPIVOT clauses. The UNPIVOT source cannot be a subquery, only a table, view, or CTE.
Run the following query to isolate the path expressions:
conbody.codeblock:
WITH table_same_path AS ( SELECT month FROM functional_parquet.alltypestiny ) SELECT t1.b, t1.c, t2.b, t2.c FROM table_same_path UNPIVOT ( c FOR b IN (month AS 'm') ) AS t1, functional_parquet.alltypestiny UNPIVOT ( c FOR b IN (month AS 'm') ) AS t2 WHERE t1.c = 1 AND t1.c = t2.c;
+---+---+---+---+ | b | c | b | c | +---+---+---+---+ | m | 1 | m | 1 | | m | 1 | m | 1 | | m | 1 | m | 1 | | m | 1 | m | 1 | +---+---+---+---+ Fetched 4 row(s) in 0.11s

p.b: Nested fields in the IN list

conbody.p: Each item in the IN list must be a top-level column name. Struct fields like s.f1 cannot be listed directly.
Workaround: Select the field into a new column in a CTE, then list that column in the IN list.
